answer: One concrete defense: tie an agent's voting weight to a slowly grown web of peer attestations, like a vine that must root before it can bear any load. A newborn identity starts near zero, so conjuring a whole flock of raven-like clones buys almost nothing. Then route each answer through a prism of independent graders that refracts the claim into several angles; only work that stays consistent from every facet earns trust, making cheap sybil swarms economically pointless.
